predecessors.name: Ottoman Empire
predecessors.text: northern Yemen, which Imam Yahya 'declared ... to be independent' on the Ottoman collapse; the infobox lists the Yemen Vilayet as the preceding state

successors.name: Republic of Yemen
successors.text: North Yemen's territory in the unification of 22 May 1990, with the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen

ledger.x: 30 October 1918: Imam Yahya's northern Yemen becomes independent of the Ottoman Empire.
1922: Imam Yahya attacks Aden.
1922: the advance on Aden is turned back by British air attacks; in 1934 Yahya 'signed a friendship treaty with the United Kingdom' promising not to attack Aden.
Hodeidah returns to Yemen.
Najran and the frontier strip go to the Saudis in Cliopatria's 1932 shape.
November 1933: the Yemenis advance on Najran.
May 1934: Saudi forces occupy the Yemeni Tihamah.
14 June 1934: the Treaty of Taif ends the war.
14 June 1934: Yemen cedes Asir, Najran and Jizan.
7 July 1934: the last Saudi troops leave Yemen after the Treaty of Taif, ending the Saudi occupation of Hajara, Luhayya and Hodeidah.
1948: the capital moves from Sanaa to Taiz.
26 September 1962: the Mutawakkilite Kingdom becomes the Yemen Arab Republic.
26 September 1962: the revolution restores Sanaa as the capital.
26 September 1962: the North Yemen Civil War begins between the republic and the royalists of the deposed imam, backed by Saudi Arabia and Jordan; Egypt backed the republic.

25 February 1963: Egyptian and republican forces occupy Marib in the Ramadan Offensive; 'On February 25, the forces occupied Marib, and on March 7 they took Harib', and the royalist commander at Harib withdrew to Beihan.
16 July 1965: the royalists retake Marib.
November 1967: the royalists besiege Sanaa.
February 1968: the siege of Sanaa is lifted.
1 December 1970: the civil war ends.
22 May 1990: North and South Yemen unite.
22 May 1990: North Yemen ends in the Republic of Yemen.

wars.name: Yemeni attack on Aden
wars.outcome: Yahya's forces reached within 50 km of Aden and were forced back by British air attacks; no border changed.

wars.name: 1931 Saudi-Yemeni border skirmish
wars.outcome: A clash of frontier guards at 'Aru early in 1931; the page's table has 'Military outcome unclear; Status quo ante bellum'.

wars.name: Saudi-Yemeni war (1934)
wars.outcome: The Saudis took Hajara (7 April), Najran (21 April), Luhayya (1 May) and Hodeidah (4 May 1934); the Treaty of Taif (14 June 1934) gave Asir, Najran and Jizan to Saudi Arabia, returned Hajjah and Hodeidah to Yemen and demarcated the border; the last Saudi…

wars.name: North Yemen Civil War
wars.outcome: The republicans, helped by Egypt, defeated the royalists, who were backed by Saudi Arabia and Jordan; Egypt recalled 15,000 troops in August 1967, the siege of Sanaa was lifted by February 1968, Saudi Arabia recognized the republic in 1970 and the infobox…

wars.name: Yemenite War of 1972
wars.outcome: After the war 'the two states declared that unification would eventually occur'; no border change.

wars.name: Yemenite War of 1979
wars.outcome: The Arab League intervened to stop it; the unification plans 'were put on hold due to the Yemenite War of 1979'; no border change.

certainty.note: Tribal highland frontiers: the Aden Protectorate border and the Najran and Asir frontier are not fixed by any page opened.
The Treaty of Taif (14 June 1934) demarcated the border with Saudi Arabia, so the northern frontier is sharp from 1934; the southern frontier with the Aden Protectorate and South Yemen stays soft.
